subject: Cloud Computing
title: Right-Sizing Resources
description: A short lesson to help you apply Right-Sizing Resources.

hook.text: A team runs 50 servers with 16 CPUs each. Average utilization: 5%. They're paying for 95% empty space.

buildup.text: Right-sizing means matching resource allocation to actual usage. Use smaller instances when demand is low.

discovery.text: Cloud providers offer tools to analyze usage: AWS Compute Optimizer, Azure Advisor, GCP Recommender.

twist.text: Teams resist right-sizing because smaller instances feel risky. 'What if we need the capacity?' they say.

climax.text: Combining right-sizing with auto-scaling gives you both: low costs normally and capacity when you need it.

punchline.text: Don't pay for resources you're not using. Right-size first.

quiz.question: What is right-sizing in cloud cost management?
options: Matching resource allocation to actual usage patterns to eliminate waste
Always choosing the largest available instance for maximum performance
Shutting down all cloud resources during off-peak hours

details.summary: Right-sizing matches instance types and sizes to actual workload requirements. Most cloud instances are over-provisioned because teams choose sizes based on peak estimates rather than measured usage. Right-sizing can cut compute costs by 30 to 50 percent.
details.whyItMatters: Over-provisioning is the single largest source of cloud waste. Right-sizing is the easiest cost optimization because it reduces waste without changing architecture.
takeaways: Most instances are over-provisioned for their actual workload
Right-sizing can reduce compute costs by 30 to 50 percent
Requires monitoring actual CPU, memory, and network utilization

faq.question: How do you identify over-provisioned instances?
faq.answer: Monitor CPU, memory, network, and disk utilization over at least two weeks. Instances consistently below 20 percent CPU are strong candidates for downsizing. AWS Compute Optimizer and Azure Advisor provide automated right-sizing recommendations.

faq.question: How often should you right-size?
faq.answer: Review quarterly or after significant application changes. Traffic patterns, code optimizations, and feature launches all change resource requirements. Continuous monitoring and automated recommendations make right-sizing an ongoing process rather than a one-time exercise.
